statutes.act: Read With Section 34 Of The Indian Penal Code

facts: The Order of the Court was as follows :

Being aggrieved and dissatisfied by the judgment and order dated 26.6.1998 passed by the Gwalior Bench of Madhya Pradesh High Court in Criminal Appeal No. 276/82 confirming the conviction order passed by the Vth Addl. Sessions Judge, Gwalior in S.T. No. 88/82, the accused-appellants preferred the special leave petition before this Court.
The Addl. Sessions Judge arrived at the conclusion that accused were guilty for the offence punishable under Section 302 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code.
Undisputedly, the incident took place on 12.4.1981 where it is stated that death of Talat Nasreen occurred in the house of accused persons in the ground floor.
For our purpose, it is not necessary to discuss the entire evidence because this appeal is confined only with regard to the role played by the appellant-Nazra.

Prosecution has also led evidence to the effect that before few days of the incident, the appellant uttered the words that if the said articles are not given then the deceased would not go alive from their house.

The prosecution has produced on record the evidence of Smt. Shanta Singhal (PW-24) who has specifically stated that the appellant was a staff Nurse in J.A. Group of Hospitals at Gwalior and on 12.4.1981 she was on duty from 1 p.m. to 7 p.m. and to that effect there is entry in the duty register.

Considering the aforesaid evidence on record, in our view, it is difficult to arrive at the conclusion that the appellant is guilty for the offence punishable under Section 302 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code.
petitioner_arguments: The appeal is allowed, impugned order passed by the High Court confirming the conviction of the appellant is set aside. Appellant is acquitted for the offence for which she was convicted. Appellant be released forthwith, if she is not re-quired in any other case.
court_reasoning: The evidence on record including circumstantial evidence does not in any way connect the accused with the offence punishable under Section 302 read with Section 34 IPC.

Alleged subsequent conduct of the appellant for which she is acquitted for the offence punishable under Section 201 IPC would be of no relevance for connecting the accused with the crime for which she is convicted.
holding: The appeal is allowed, impugned order passed by the High Court confirming the conviction of the appellant is set aside. Appellant is acquitted for the offence for which she was convicted. Appellant be released forthwith, if she is not re-quired in any other case.
